name: Small rail planes
question: Where should the small rails' copper go: 3V3_MAIN on the empty part of In3, on the bottom layer, or in In2's signal window?
why_now:
The 60 A path and the six outputs have their copper (D18–D21, PR #64). The four small rails have none yet: **3V3_MAIN** (74 pads, every corner of the board), **1V5_CORE** (U303 to U401's four core balls), **VBAT_FILT** (L201 to U302's input) and **VDDAU_AON** (U301 to U501). Also **VBAT_PROT** has no copper north of y 71 since In3 was cut to the power band, so L201 and U301, which take their input from it, are not joined at all.

Since PR #64, In3 is VBAT_PROT only in the band x 72–238, y 71–122. The rest of In3 is empty, and tracks are not allowed on it (POWER_ONLY_In3). That empty copper is the natural home for 3V3_MAIN, but you cut In3 for your own reasons, so I'm not assuming it's free. That is the question.

I drew option A on a copy of main's board (`power_shapes.json` + `draw_power.py`, which now also places one via per small-rail pad and U401's dogbones), filled it, ran DRC and measured it with `copper_r.py`. B and C are judged from the routing numbers, not drawn.

facts.label: Rails
facts.value: 3V3_MAIN from U302 (LMQ66430, 3 A rating) through R302; 1V5_CORE from U303 (TPS628502, 2 A) through R303; VDDAU_AON from U301 (TPS7B8133) through R301; VBAT_FILT from L201 (sized for 2.1 A worst case). There is no 3V3 load budget yet

facts.label: Design loads used
facts.value: 3V3_MAIN 1.33 A in all: U303's input 1.0 A (2 A × 1.5 V ÷ 3.3 V ÷ 0.9), U401 0.2 A, U501 0.1 A, the rest small. 1V5_CORE at U303's full 2 A. Assumed, so you can read the drops off proportionally

facts.label: Stackup
facts.value: In2 is 0.311 mm from In3 and 0.55 mm from In1, so In3 is the nearer reference plane for In2's signals. B.Cu signals reference In4 (GND), F.Cu signals In1 (GND)

facts.label: Routing load
facts.value: Joining 3V3_MAIN by tracks takes 73 of the board's 333 pad-to-pad connections (spanning tree); on a plane those 73 go away

facts.label: Vias
facts.value: Filled and capped (DEC-027), so a via may sit in a pad: 0.40/0.20 mm (a preset) in every small-rail pad that holds it, else beside the pad with a 0.3 mm stub. U401's power and ground balls get dogbones at the diagonal cell centres (0.8 mm pitch, 0.10 mm escape clearance)

facts.label: Handbook
facts.value: Says nothing on plane splits or via-in-pad, so nothing here disagrees with it

options.name: 3V3_MAIN on In3, north of the band
options.summary: In3 north of y 70.8, across the whole width, becomes one 3V3_MAIN plane. Inside it sit a 1V5_CORE island (U401's core box, then a 1.2 mm strip east and north to R303 and TP303) and two VBAT_PROT fingers from the band north to L201 (3.2 mm wide) and U301/C301 (1.2 mm). VBAT_FILT is a small pour on B from L201's pad 2 to C305, C304, C303 and U302, plus one on F joining C207 and C217 over L201. VDDAU_AON stays a track: four pads within 4 mm, a few mA, inside U501's escape area. Below y 71, R601, R701 and R801 are all fed 3V3 by track, the same way, so the six outputs stay alike.

images.caption: In3 from above: 3V3_MAIN (red) north of the band, the 1V5_CORE island (green) at U401, the VBAT_PROT band and its two fingers (blue)
U401: dogbones (dots) and the 1V5_CORE island running to R303. The top-side caps under the BGA don't line up with the via grid, which is repair R3
L201 and U302: the VBAT_PROT finger and its five vias (two in L201's pad 1, three under C207's body); VBAT_FILT on B and F, joined through two vias in L201's pad 2 under C217's pad

measures.label: 3V3_MAIN drop, R302 to each load
measures.value: U303 input 5.3 mV, U401 balls 3.8 mV, U501 decaps 3.0 mV, others ≤ 4.2 mV; 6 mW in all. About half is R302's one via, and more vias there would cut it

measures.label: 1V5_CORE drop, R303 to the core balls
measures.value: 26 mV at 2 A (52 mW); about 4 mV at a likely 0.3 A

measures.label: In3 copper
measures.value: 3V3_MAIN 8,732 mm²; VBAT_PROT 6,653 mm² (6,537 + 116 of fingers); band loss unchanged

measures.label: Reference for In2's signals
measures.value: Solid 3V3_MAIN under the whole signal window, except the 1V5 strip at U401 (1.2 mm, x 208–209)

measures.label: DRC on the copy
measures.value: 1 clearance and 1 hole-clearance error, both at C410 under U401 (repair R3); parity 0

measures.label: Vias added
measures.value: 30 dogbones (H10 and J6 have no free cell, repair R3), 36 pad vias, 9 VBAT_PROT and 2 VBAT_FILT in fields

gains: Uses copper that is empty today; no outer-layer room taken
73 fewer connections for you to route
In2's signal window keeps a solid plane under it
costs: In3 north is committed to 3V3_MAIN, so it can't become a signal window later without a re-draw
The 1V5 strip makes the 3V3 current to U303 go around it, south of U401 (included in the 5.3 mV)

options.name: Small rails on B.Cu, In3 north left empty
options.summary: 3V3_MAIN, 1V5_CORE and VBAT_FILT as pours and wide tracks on B (and F where the parts are on top). In3 north stays empty. Not drawn: nearly every part is on B, so a B pour is cut by every track you route, and its shape only settles after your routing.

images.caption: B.Cu: the 74 3V3_MAIN pads (red) a bottom-layer rail would have to reach, among the bottom-side parts

measures.label: 3V3_MAIN drop, R302 to each load
measures.value: Not measurable until routed; a 0.4 mm PWR_RAIL track across 100 mm is about 0.15 Ω at 85 °C, so 0.15 V at 1 A

measures.label: 1V5_CORE drop, R303 to the core balls
measures.value: U401's core balls are inside the ball field on B; the strip would have to go on F, round J401 and the top-side caps

measures.label: Reference for In2's signals
measures.value: No plane on In3 north (In1 GND is 0.55 mm away)

gains: In3 north stays free for something else
costs: Takes the bottom layer's room, where you route

options.name: 3V3_MAIN in In2's signal window
options.summary: Pour 3V3_MAIN on In2 north of y 70, where D17 A opened In2 to signals, and keep In3 north empty or GND.

measures.label: 3V3_MAIN drop, R302 to each load
measures.value: about as A (same area, same thickness)

measures.label: Pad-to-pad connections left to route
measures.value: 260, but with In2 north gone. Without that window about 35 nets did not route (D17)

gains: In3 north could become GND under In2
costs: Reverses D17 A and gives back the routing failures it fixed

recommendation.why:
A puts the small rails on copper that does nothing today. It takes 73 connections off your routing and leaves B and F to you. The drops are a few millivolts at loads I've likely overstated. B spends the layer you route on, and C undoes D17 A.

Whichever you pick, the trial found three placement problems. I recommend fixing all of them; each is a small pose change, and I'd show you the result before it lands:

**R1.** C206 is the EMI filter's output cap (4.7 µF, 100 V, on VBAT_FILT). It sits at (146, 32.5), 34 mm from L201 and U302, so it does little as a filter cap and drags VBAT_FILT across the board. Move it beside L201's pad 2 and C305, and bring TP205 (VBAT_FILT's second test point, at 132.6, 73.3) next to it.

**R2.** C405 (4.7 µF on 1V5_CORE) sits at (211.9, 65.6), 14 mm south of U401's core and off the 1V5 island. Move it beside the island's strip at U401's east edge.

**R3.** The top-side caps under U401 (C401–C404, C406–C415, C417–C423) were placed without the via grid. Two balls (H10 on 1V5_CORE, J6 on GND) have no free diagonal cell, and C410's GND pad is too close to a 3V3_MAIN dogbone. Re-pose them so each cap's pads sit on its own rail's dogbone vias. That becomes a pose table for U401's decoupling, which comes back to you as a block.

Left to your hand routing in every option: the 3V3 feeds into the power band (R601/R607, R701/R707, R801/R807, U202, C214, C215, R211, U203), U501's three 3V3 pins and VDDAU_AON, U302's and U303's pins to their own caps (the hot loops), the caps under U401 to their via tops, and Q501, Q502 and C513, which found no via site.

answer: Reply with A, B or C, and which of R1–R3 to make (for example "A, all three"). On A, I draw it on main's board in a PR: the In3 3V3_MAIN plane, the 1V5_CORE island, the VBAT_PROT fingers, the VBAT_FILT pours and the vias, through power_shapes.json. CLAUDE.md's layer-role line and the log get updated in the same PR. The repairs come first, as poses you see before they land.
